706192.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- Proto-Indo-European *-s Proto-Indo-European *dʰéh₁s Proto-Indo-European *dʰh₁sós Proto-Hellenic *tʰehós Ancient Greek θεός From Proto-Hellenic *tʰehós (whence also Mycenaean Greek 𐀳𐀃 (te-o)), a thematicization of…

706178.t: From τίθημι (tĭ́thēmĭ, “to set, put, place”) + -μα (-mă, nominal suffix), and/or directly from Proto-Indo-European *dʰéh₁mn̥, leveled to the weak stem *dʰh₁-. Doublet of θῆμα (thêmă) and θημών (thēmṓn).

706103.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tʰə́pt͏̌ō, perhaps from a Proto-Indo-European *dʰm̥bʰyéti, from *dʰembʰ- (“to dig”), with cognates including Old Armenian դամբան (damban, “tomb”) and possibly Avestan 𐬛𐬀𐬑𐬨𐬀 (daxma), Middle Persian [script needed] (dhmk'), Old Prussian…

706145.t: May have been first Proto-Hellenic *tʰāwéomai/*tʰāwáomai, perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₂w-. Alternatively, Beekes takes the word and its relatives as Pre-Greek, see θαῦμα (thaûma) for more.

706138.t: From θαυμάζω (thaumázō, “to admire, be surprised at”) + -τός (-tós, adjective suffix).

706134.t: Traditionally derived from a Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₂w- (whence θεάομαι (theáomai), θῆβος (thêbos), θήγεια (thḗgeia)), an extension of *dʰeh₂-, with no clear cognates outside Hellenic; other extensions include θάμβος (thámbos) (< *dʰh₂n̥bʰos), τάφος…

706126.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dʰers- (“to dare”). Cognate with English dare, Proto-Slavic *dьrzъ (“bold”), Sanskrit धृषु (dhṛṣú, “proud”) and Albanian nder (“honor, favour”).

706184.t: From the stem of τίθημι (títhēmi, “to place”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁-, possibly combined with the stem of ἵστημι (hístēmi, “to stand”), from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂-.

706195.t: From θεός (theós) + τίκτω (tíktō, “to bear”) + -ος (-os), by ellipsis of a noun like γῆ f (gê, “land, country”). Probably a translation from an Egyptian epithet with sense "birthplace of every god".
